description: Registry work types whose objects carry no abstract and no prose. THE CLAIM IS NOT "this is not a replication" — it is that there is nothing here to screen and nothing to code an outcome from, so the object cannot become a FLoRA record whatever it is the artifact of. Stating it that way is what makes it defensible: a deposit is not asserted to be off-topic, it is asserted to be uncodable. Scope ruling by the maintainer, 2026-08-04. `component` and `database` are on the list on the same argument and are the two worth a second look (D4): a `component` can occasionally be an independently meaningful report. The residual risk is real: where a deposit is the ONLY record of a replication, that replication is lost. The mitigation would be a linkage worklist rather than an admission — record the deposit's parent DOI, check whether the parent is in the pool, route the unlinked remainder to a human — deferred to #157.

measured.rationale: Structural and scope, not statistical. Every type on this list names a registry object that carries no abstract and no prose, and the discard claims exactly that: there is no text to screen and no text to code an outcome from. A precision sample would answer a different question (how often such an object is the artifact OF a replication), which the ruling deliberately does not turn on. What a sample IS still owed for is the residual loss — the deposit that is the only record of its replication — and that is the V1 parent-recovery measurement (proposal SS7), deferred with #157. Supersedes the retired `dataset-type` spec, whose 2026-08-03 pilot evidence measured screen spend (69.8% of dataset rows proceed in the concept arm vs 12.5% for articles) rather than precision and therefore could not license a live discard on a not-a-replication claim; the v2 rule discards on the uncodable-text claim instead.
